warnings: Simulation correctness (highest priority): ensure the fluid domain is truly LIQUID and that the liquid surface mesh is enabled + baked. Verify you are rendering the liquid mesh, not the domain bounds/volume cache. If your cache output is VDB “fluid_data_####.vdb”, you may be baking a gas/smoke cache—fix domain_type and rebake from scratch.

Enable/boost secondary particles for spray: turn on Spray/Foam/Mist (as needed), and render them with instanced tiny spheres or a dedicated droplet material; increase particle amount gradually (start low, then scale up).

Emitter shaping: use plane-init inflow but add breakup (inflow noise / slight angular spread) so the fan becomes droplets after a short distance; keep velocity in the 2–3 m/s range but add variation so it doesn’t form a uniform sheet.

Shading: use a physically plausible water shader (Transmission=1, IOR≈1.333, very low roughness ~0.01–0.03). Add subtle volume absorption to avoid milky/flat appearance and ensure enough refraction/transmission bounces.

Lighting: add a strong, cool rim/key light or HDRI so the spray catches sharp specular highlights (the “silvery-white” look). Increase contrast/exposure to make droplets readable against the dim basement.
Kill banding: if any volume is being rendered, reduce volume step rate / increase resolution. Prefer surface mesh for liquid; output 16/32-bit (EXR) during lookdev to avoid posterization.
Grounding: increase floor wetness response—ensure puddle is thin and glossy with clear reflections; add contact shadows/AO so water reads as touching the floor.
